name: tera-labelled-loops
instr:
Please add labelled loops to Tera 2 in `/app`, so templates can inspect and control an enclosing loop without mixing it up with the innermost one. Use the existing `tera::Tera` template API (`add_raw_template`, `render`, `render_str`, and `one_off`); no new Rust API is needed. Don't add new crates.

A loop can end its opening tag with `as name`, for example `{% for x in xs as rows %}` or `{% for k, v in items as rows %}`. Within its body, `rows.index`, `rows.index0`, `rows.first`, `rows.last`, and `rows.length` mean the same fields as `loop` but for that named loop, even inside nested loops or list comprehensions. A label is not a value: only these dot-field accesses are allowed. Labels shadow ordinary variables of the same name in their body and disappear before the loop's `else`. Labels are lexical, so an included template does not inherit its caller's labels.

`{% break rows %}` and `{% continue rows %}` target that enclosing labelled loop. They discard every intervening loop and its local variables, skipping those loops' `else` bodies; the target then behaves like a bare `break` or `continue` written directly in its own body. For example, `{% for x in [1,2] as rows %}{% for y in [3] %}{{ x }}{% continue rows %}{% endfor %}{% endfor %}` renders `12`.

A label must be an identifier, not one of Tera's reserved names or either binding of its own loop, and cannot duplicate another active label. Unknown jump labels and jumps that cross a filter section, set block, or component
